content:
Apple has confirmed it will hold a special product launch event next Tuesday (October 13) called "Welcome home," but has yet to reveal whether there will be a keynote video. Here's what we know so far.

Apple has not announced any plans for a "Welcome home" keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an "online video announcement."

Apple changed its approach to product launches this year. The March launch of the MacBook Neo was the first example — instead of holding a traditional launch event, Apple held an in-person media "experience event" after rolling out other products via press releases over consecutive days.

Now Apple's "Welcome home" event (October 13) appears set to break new ground in the same way.

Unlike traditional events, Apple has not added the "Welcome home" event to its Apple Events page, and there are no signs of a livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

Things could still change in the days leading up to the event, but current signs point to no keynote video on October 13.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says there will be a video announcement. In an article about Apple's October 27 event, Gurman wrote:

According to Gurman — who previously accurately disclosed both the October 13 date and the focus on home products — Apple will be rolling out an "online video announcement" next week.

Media have been invited to attend an "Apple Experience" event in New York City, starting at 9 a.m. Eastern Time. So if there is an announcement video, expect it to go live around then — much earlier than the usual keynote time slot.

We expect at least three new products to debut on Tuesday — see this article for details.

What do you think — will Apple release a keynote video for the "Welcome home" event? Share your thoughts in the comments.
